root_cause.text: On UP kernels, `spin_trylock()` acts as a no-op that unconditionally succeeds, enabling `kmalloc_nolock()` invoked from NMI context to re-enter the slab allocator and corrupt `n->list_lock` state.
root_cause.evidence: The CVE description explicitly states "On UP kernels (!CONFIG_SMP), spin_trylock() is a no-op that unconditionally succeeds even when the lock is already held," and the patch fixes this by adding a guard `if (!IS_ENABLED(CONFIG_SMP) && in_nmi()) return NULL;` in `mm/slub.c::kmalloc_nolock_noprof`.

intent_record.intent_summary: Fixes potential deadlock risks in NMI context on UP systems by blocking kmalloc calls where spin_trylock behavior is unreliable.
intent_record.what: Added a conditional check returning NULL if the kernel configuration indicates a uniprocessor (UP) system and execution is currently in a Non-Maskable Interrupt (NMI) context.
intent_record.how: Prevents memory allocation attempts in NMI context on UP systems, avoiding potential deadlocks or corruption caused by spin_trylock semantics that incorrectly report success on single-core architectures.
